references.text: The Lord's anger burns again against the people later in the same chapter, showing a pattern of God's judgment over Israel's complaints
The people complain again to the Lord, and this pattern of discontent repeats throughout the wilderness journey
The Israelites grumble against Moses and Aaron in the wilderness, an early example of the people's complaints during their journey
Moses reminds the people of Taberah, the place named after the fire that burned among them
Fire goes out from the Lord and consumes rebels, a similar judgment by fire as at Taberah
Fire goes out from the presence of the Lord and consumes Nadab and Abihu, a parallel to God's fire as judgment
The psalm describes how the Lord heard and became angry, and fire flamed up against Jacob - a poetic retelling of this event
The psalm mentions that fire burned in their assembly, a reference to God's judgment in the wilderness
Paul warns against grumbling as some of the Israelites did and were killed by the destroyer
Hebrews refers to the wilderness generation who sinned and were not allowed to enter rest because of unbelief
